name: zlib 1.x deflate (stock zlib) as the encoder-replay reference
purpose: Re-compress a candidate's decoded output and require byte-identity with the candidate stream (GAP-154 replay oracle); also identifies producer encoder parameters (level 6, memLevel sweep).
version: 1.3 tested (CPython zlib runtime); latest tag v1.3.2
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 timeout 1500 nice -n 10 python3 c9_replay_correct.py /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf results/c9_replay_correct --every 3 --workers 2` -> summary 'orig_replayable': 266 of 266 saveas, '"zlib": "1.3"' (results/c9_replay_correct.summary.json). Also ran 2026-09-27: encoder_sweep.py -> 2,074/2,074 saveas streams reproduced (results/encoder_sweep.summary.json). The v1.3.2 tag date is from a blobless `git fetch --depth 1` of refs/tags/v1.3.2. Not checked: whether 1.3.2 output equals 1.3's, which Stage 4 should confirm.
rationale: Serves GAP-154, GAP-052 and GAP-150 (OBS-0901, OBS-0903, OBS-0904). It reproduces 100% of Word Save As streams once memLevel is swept (OBS-0901), against the 54% the plan assumed (OBS-0303). Plan assumption changed: replay is a strong oracle for Save As but NOT a uniqueness certificate. In OBS-0903 three single-byte candidates passed inflate, Adler-32 and replay. In OBS-0904, 10.6% of damaged Save As bodies are themselves canonical zlib, so a trailer rewrite passes all three oracles. Adopt it as one independent check under charter grade 3, together with a content grammar check and exhaustive multiplicity (trailer included). Its coverage of Print to PDF is near zero (1/1,264). In the shipped binary it would conflict with the pure-Rust decision, but preflate-rs's predictor reproduces 395/400 of the same streams in pure Rust (TOOL-476, OBS-0908). Keep stock zlib as the research-side reference that the Rust path is measured against.

Version and date are from crates.io/api/v1/crates/libz-rs-sys, fetched 2026-10-05.
rationale: Hold for the replay-oracle role. It reproduced 0 of 400 stock-zlib Save As streams at identical parameters, and its output equals zlib-ng's on 380 of 400 (OBS-0902). It is a fine inflater (round-trips 400/400), and decoders are agent B's scope. Plan assumption changed: the product decision 'pure Rust, no compiled C' plus GAP-154/HYP-150 implicitly assumed a Rust crate could replay producer output. General-purpose Rust encoders cannot. preflate-rs's predictor can, with zero corrections and zlib-6 parameters (395/400, OBS-0908, TOOL-476), so a new zlib port is no longer needed.

name: Two-dummy-dictionary resync (Adler's salvage method)
purpose: Restart inflate at a bit offset after lost history; mark bytes identical under two different 32 KiB dummy dictionaries as independent of the lost history (CLM-0337, SRC-0313).
verification_evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/dict_resync.summary.json): `nice python3 dict_resync.py /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf results/dict_resync --max-streams 300` -> 'precision_reliable': 1.0, 'blind_scan_false_starts_total': 51120, 'blind_scan_reliable_but_wrong_bytes_total': 8521181. It needs only CPython zlib 1.3, which is present after the 2026-10-05 restart; not re-run.
rationale: Serves GAP-152, GAP-151 and DMG-003 (OBS-0900). At a true block boundary it is exact (precision 1.0, median recall 0.82). A blind bit-offset scan, which is how SRC-0313's salvage finds starts, produced 8.5M bytes that both dictionaries agree on yet are wrong. Requiring the last block to end exactly at the Adler-32 trailer removed all 51,120 false starts and kept 60% of true starts. Plan assumption changed: charter grade 2 ('output identical under two different dummy dictionaries') is unsafe as written. It needs a confirmed restart, by trailer alignment or a following block that decodes. Applies only to multi-block streams (print font and content streams), since PR #16 found most streams single-block.
alternatives: Brown 2013 intra-block resync with known Huffman tables (PR #16; ZipRec GPL)

name: Replay-guided single-byte Flate corrector (prototype c9_replay_correct.py)

verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 timeout 1500 nice -n 10 python3 c9_replay_correct.py /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf results/c9_replay_correct --every 3 --workers 2` -> saveas 'method_unique_replay_correct': 196 of 266, 'method_wrong_replay_candidates': 1, wall 723.9 s.
rationale: Serves GAP-150, GAP-154, GAP-052 and GAP-253 (OBS-0903, OBS-0904). Replay localisation helps Save As streams (196/266) but does nothing for print, and Adler-32 algebra localisation is weak (21/317). PR #16's grammar localizer and checkpointed search score higher (324/343, 218/221). Trial it only as the replay arm inside PR #16's ladder. Plan assumption changed: §4.5/§16 single-byte salvage must (1) enumerate every candidate, trailer edits included, (2) require a grammar check, and (3) mark differing bytes indeterminate when more than one survives (CLM-0105). Windowed search can emit a wrong 'unique' candidate.

name: Closed-form xref deletion solver (prototype xref_constraints.py)

purpose: Recover the code-to-character map of fonts that lost ToUnicode and font program (C7/C8) as a substitution cipher, from code sequences and a character n-gram model, with per-code abstention margins.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: two shards `... decipher_codes.py /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf research/cache/fulltext .../results/decipher_codes --shard k/2` (about 600-680 s each) then `--merge 2` -> 'token_acc': 0.7657 over 192,680 tokens; 'digit_acc': 0.0652; 'margin>10': coverage 0.8682, acc_on_kept 0.8629 (results/decipher_codes.summary.json).
rationale: Serves GAP-205, GAP-201 and GAP-003 (OBS-0906, OBS-0907). This is the first PDF decipherment measurement. Search SRCH-0901 found no prior tool, and PR #16 found none either. Accuracy reaches 0.86 on long Latin slots, but digits are 6.5% and slots under 256 codes are 0.44-0.49. Plan assumption changed: RQ3 'without a language prior inventing it' becomes measurable. Decipherment gives a grade-4 inference with per-code margins and abstention. Digits need non-linguistic evidence (widths, glyph order, numeric context). Add PR #16 width fingerprints and per-script LMs in the trial.

name: preflate-rs token predictor as a zero-correction replay oracle
purpose: Pure-Rust encoder replay: re-encode a candidate plaintext under a producer's DEFLATE parameters with no corrections and compare it with the damaged stream (GAP-154). The same crate's correction size is a soft signal where exact replay is impossible.
verification_evidence: 2026-10-05: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$S/cargo-target cargo build --release -j2 && $S/cargo-target/release/preflate_probe $S/pf_sample --replay` (experiments/preflate_probe) -> summary 'saveas_zero_correction_replay': 'zlib6_params_exact': 395 of 400 ('8': 220, '7': 175), 'own_estimated_params_exact': 47; print 0 of 400; '# preflate-rs panics caught: 14' (results/preflate_probe.summary.json). Version and date from crates.io/api/v1/crates/preflate-rs; licence from the repository LICENSE (Apache License 2.0) via raw.githubusercontent.com and crates.io metadata; tag v0.7.6 via git ls-remote; all fetched 2026-10-05.
rationale: Serves GAP-154, GAP-150 and GAP-052 (OBS-0908, OBS-0902, OBS-0901). It is the only pure-Rust path found that replays Word Save As streams byte-for-byte (395/400, against 0/400 for zlib-rs and 5/400 for miniz_oxide). Plan assumption changed: the conflict between the pure-Rust product decision and the replay oracle (TOOL-450/451) mostly dissolves. No new zlib port is needed. A producer profile must supply the parameters (memLevel 7 or 8; per-stream estimates replay only 47/399). Three blockers remain for the Trial. First, the replay entry point needs a crate API or fork, because the probe mirrors a private struct. Second, forced parameters can panic (14 in this run), so the code needs catch_unwind or a fix. Third, the 4 memLevel-7 misses are unexplained. It does not help Print to PDF, where only correction size is available as a damage and localisation signal (TOOL-366 measured that; untested here). Replay is still not a uniqueness certificate (OBS-0903/0904).
alternatives: TOOL-450 stock zlib 1.x (C; exact on 400/400 but conflicts with pure Rust)
TOOL-451 zlib-rs and TOOL-452 miniz_oxide (not byte-compatible)
TOOL-366 preflate-rs round trip with corrections (same crate, different use)
a new Rust port of zlib 1.x deflate_slow (now unnecessary unless the misses matter)
